Q138869462.summary: Christ, seen from behind, rises up a channel of cloud and grasps the hand of God reaching down from heaven, while rows of figures look on from the clouds at either side. Below, two angels gesture down to the Virgin and the apostles, who crowd together in vivid gestures of wonder. Framed by a deep acanthus border, this ivory once adorned the cover of a liturgical book, presenting the Ascension as the triumphant return of the Son to the Father.
facts: The Kunsthistorisches Museum dates the plaque to the end of the 10th century and attributes it, with a query, to Metz.
The museum notes that the elegant acanthus frieze and parts of the composition follow Byzantine models.
Showing Christ from behind being drawn up by the hand of God is a distinctive Western way of representing the Ascension.
Q138869462.notes: Inv. Kunstkammer 7284; 20.6 × 14.4 cm. Date was '900s'; the museum gives 'Ende 10. Jh.'. The third fact is a general iconographic observation, not from the museum text.
